problem_type: settings surface semantic and validation-boundary regression
symptom: The File & saving page mixed generated-file auto-save controls with the project location used for cross-device continuation, while the visible Check folder action only re-read settings and could not prove that the configured folder was usable.
direct_cause: SettingsDialog rendered two unrelated storage concepts in one first-view flow, and ProjectLocationSection called projectLocation.get() for its check action instead of a filesystem validation operation.
class_root: The settings surface had no shared invariant separating project-location configuration from optional artifact export, and no dedicated validation contract for user-facing folder health. As a result, copy, layout, and behavior could drift independently while still passing shape-only UI checks.
affected_population: Every user looking for a place to continue editing on another computer
Users with a missing, replaced, non-directory, or non-writable configured project folder
Users reading the File & saving page in Chinese or English and either light or dark theme
entry_points: Check folder action through the renderer bridge and trusted IPC handler

external_sources.purpose: Provide a verified external destination for users who need a third-party folder synchronization tool; Nomi does not configure or claim transfer state for that tool.
Provide a verified Nutstore download destination in the expanded three-step guidance.

internal_only_reason: The semantic separation and folder-health claim are Nomi-owned invariants; third-party sync websites only provide optional destinations and cannot define the Settings component hierarchy or local validation contract.
invariants: The File & saving first view exposes one project-location owner for new-project defaults; unrelated generated-artifact auto-save controls are not rendered in that surface.
Cross-device guidance is a separate semantic section with one short collapsed hint and an optional three-step disclosure; it never claims that Nomi performed synchronization.
Check folder invokes the shared project-location validation boundary and fails with an allowlisted error when the path is not a directory or is not writable.
Chinese and English use the same component tree, existing DesignButton and token classes, and the same light/dark layout hierarchy.
generality_proof: Every user-visible project-location action enters ProjectLocationSection, and every renderer check crosses the single project-location bridge into the trusted IPC registration. Separating the sections at SettingsDialog and validating at the shared IPC boundary prevents another caller from reintroducing the mixed storage concept or a read-only check.

shared_boundaries.responsibility: Own the File & saving information hierarchy and render only the project-location feature on this page.
Own project path actions, the collapsed/expanded continuation guidance, and the single Check folder affordance.
Validate the configured path and write probe at the trusted filesystem boundary before reporting it usable.

same_class_entry_points.evidence: The action now calls the dedicated bridge check operation rather than the read-only get operation.
Picker and reveal already validate the same root at the filesystem boundary; the new check operation reuses that validator.
This runtime still serves generation output behavior and is not a settings-surface project-location owner; removing its settings controls does not change its generation contract.

recurrence.reason: Settings pages can repeatedly conflate adjacent storage features, and any future status action can regress to a read-only refresh unless the behavior is represented by a dedicated bridge operation and shared validation boundary.
same_class_scan: Searched SettingsDialog, ProjectLocationSection, preload, DesktopSettingsBridge, and projectLocation IPC for every project-location and auto-save entry point.
Checked the existing picker and reveal paths to confirm they use filesystem validation before mutation or reveal.
Ran the settings structural test and project-location IPC tests after the new handler and section split.

prevention.invariant: A folder health claim is returned only after validateProjectLocationRoot succeeds through the dedicated check operation.
prevention.failure_mode: Invalid or unwritable paths return an allowlisted error and never report the folder usable.
prevention.strategy: Keep UI actions thin and route every folder-health check through one trusted IPC function that reuses the existing validator.

legacy_paths.rationale: The obsolete settings UI and its locale copy are removed; the generation-time auto-save runtime remains because it is a separate existing capability outside this surface.

dependency_lifecycle.rationale: The invariant uses Electron IPC and Node filesystem primitives already owned by Nomi; no third-party dependency controls folder validation.

migration: Existing auto-save preferences remain stored for the generation runtime but are no longer presented in Settings → File & saving. Existing project-location settings are read unchanged and are validated on explicit Check folder.
residual_risks: Nomi can validate the local folder but cannot prove that VerySync, Nutstore, or another external client has completed transfer.
A real two-computer network transfer and continuation task still requires a second reachable computer and a configured sync client; this change does not claim that evidence.
